points.description: mRNA leaves the nucleus, e.g. through a nuclear pore.
mRNA travels through the cytoplasm to a ribosome or to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
mRNA codons are read and tRNA with the complementary anticodon binds the codon, bringing the corresponding amino acid.
Amino acids are joined into a protein chain, starting at a START codon and continuing until a STOP codon is read.

rubric.notes: Award 0.75 for each of the four steps correctly described; full marks require all four. Accept equivalent wording and correct alternative descriptions of the same step. A bare list without description does not earn the description mark for that step.
